chunks: And as for what Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā narrated from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Qummī, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Maymūn al-Qaddāḥ, from Jaʿfar, from his father: that ʿAlī عليه السلام, when salat was performed over a deceased person, would recite Sūrat al-Fātiḥah and send blessings upon the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم and his family—the rest of the hadith.
So the interpretation regarding these two reports is taqiyyah, because they are in agreement with the doctrines of some of the ʿĀmmah.

key_terms.التَّقِيَّةُ: dissimulation or precautionary concealment due to circumstances
key_terms.الْعَامَّةِ: the general Sunni populace in Shia hadith usage
key_terms.فَاتِحَةِ الْكِتَابِ: Sūrat al-Fātiḥah, the opening chapter of the Qur'an

ai.seo_question: Why are some hadiths about recitation in the funeral prayer interpreted as taqiyyah in al-Istibṣār?
ai.summary: This passage addresses two reports concerning recitation in the funeral prayer and explains them as having been issued under taqiyyah. It indicates that these reports align with the views of some among the general Sunni populace, and thus are not taken as the operative ruling.
